title: Roman consensus — all needed for eternal salvation in Scripture explicitly or in seed
source_text: VII. Et quamvis in hac quaestione omnes Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae non eodem modo loquantur, sed alii plus, & alii minus Scripturae videantur hac in re tribuere; in eo tamen omnes conveniunt, omnia quae sunt ad aeternam salutem necessario requisita, in Scriptura sacra contineri explicite, vel implicite, expresse vel virtute, & tanquam in semine, si ad eum sensum Scripturae investigantur quem intendit Spiritus sanctus.
pass_a_gloss: And although in this question all the Doctors of the Roman Church do not speak in the same way, but some seem to attribute more, and others less, to Scripture in this matter; yet in this they all agree: that all things which are necessarily required for eternal salvation are contained in sacred Scripture explicitly or implicitly, expressly or by virtue, and as it were in seed, if the Scriptures are investigated toward that sense which the Holy Spirit intends.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors do not all speak alike here — some seem to grant Scripture more, some less.

Yet they all agree: everything necessarily required for eternal salvation is in sacred Scripture explicitly or implicitly, expressly or by virtue, and as in seed — if Scripture is read in the sense the Holy Spirit intends.
